purpose: Decide how a fixed-fee monthly bookkeeping practice keeps the book it has already sold economically sound and stable: how much recurring delivery load one seat can actually carry and therefore when intake must stop, how unpriced work entering live accounts is detected and routed rather than absorbed, when and how a client's monthly fee is corrected on an announced cadence without ambush or fear-selling, how monthly reporting and the review conversation are made useful enough that the owner stays without the practice drifting into licensed tax or attest territory, how at-risk, seasonal and financially distressed clients are handled with care, when a mis-fit client is exited cleanly with records handed over and access revoked, and how referral flow from CPAs and niche communities is built inside confidentiality and professional-boundary limits.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the practice already sells a productized fixed-fee monthly subscription with defined tiers and has clients live on it; this KB governs the existing book, not the design of the offer or the sale of a new one

revenue is a fixed monthly subscription per client tier, so an hour spent beyond the priced scope is absorbed margin rather than billable time, and the only levers are client count, tier mix, fee level, cost-to-serve and retention

every capacity figure, effort estimate, fee movement, band edge and contribution number in this KB is a mechanism the practice measures inside its own book, never a market rate, benchmark table or industry statistic asserted as fact

the practice performs bookkeeping-side work only; tax returns, tax positions and planning, representation, attest and assurance engagements, and legal interpretation belong to a licensed professional and are referred out

licensing and title-use rules, engagement and notice-period contract law, records-retention and client-records-return obligations, and data-protection duties differ by jurisdiction and change over time; this KB names the obligation class and requires current rules to be verified locally with a qualified professional

the practice holds continuing access to client bank, processor, payroll and accounting-system credentials for the whole life of the subscription, so least-privilege access and confidentiality are standing operating conditions, not onboarding tasks
the same small team that sells and delivers also runs these decisions, so a retention or pricing action that cannot be delivered inside measured capacity is not a real option
exclusions: designing the tier ladder itself, defining scope per tier, selecting or committing to a niche, positioning against hourly bookkeeping and do-it-yourself software, and qualifying or pricing a prospect before an engagement exists - owned by the productized bookkeeping offer and niche selection KB
the pre-engagement sales conversation, the books-condition read at quote stage, and the decision to decline or refer a prospect who was never a client - owned by the same offer and niche selection KB

the diagnostic review and the cleanup or catch-up project, chart-of-accounts and workflow standardization, and the execution mechanics of the monthly close including feeds, reconciliation, categorization review and production of the reporting packet - owned by the client onboarding, cleanup and monthly close KB

accuracy controls inside the close and the escalation of an individual transaction-level judgment call to the client or their CPA - owned by the same onboarding and close KB; this KB owns only the relationship-level boundary and the referral relationship

attest, assurance, review and compilation engagements, tax return preparation, tax positions or planning, payroll or sales-tax filing positions, representation before any authority, and legal interpretation of engagement contracts, liens or entity structure
personalized financial, tax, legal, insurance or investment advice to a client; this KB is educational and operational and stops at the point where licensed judgment begins
invented market rates, fee benchmarks, competitor price lists, industry churn or margin statistics, capacity figures presented as universal, or market-size claims stated as fact
accounting software administration tutorials, ledger mechanics instruction, and hiring, employment-law or compensation decisions for practice staff beyond the capacity arithmetic of a delivery seat

competency_questions.question: How many live client accounts can one delivery seat carry at the promised close quality, and how do I know that number is measured rather than assumed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOOK_ECONOMICS_MODEL names the levers that move recurring revenue, RECURRING_EFFORT_LEDGER supplies the measured per-client monthly effort, and SEAT_CAPACITY_MECHANISM derives clients-per-seat from that measurement with its stated reserve and its recheck condition

competency_questions.question: Which clients in the current book are carrying themselves and which are being subsidised by the rest?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLIENT_CONTRIBUTION_VIEW states how measured effort and the client's fee are put side by side per month, how shared overhead is treated, and what the practice does with an account that stays underwater for consecutive cycles

competency_questions.question: When must I stop admitting new subscription clients, and what happens to the demand I cannot serve this month?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INTAKE_ADMISSION_GATE states the capacity ceiling test and the deferral path, and WORKLOAD_CALENDAR_SMOOTHING shows why the ceiling is about the shape of the month and the year, not just the client count

competency_questions.question: How do I see unpriced work entering a live account before it becomes the new normal, and where does that work go once I have seen it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCOPE_DRIFT_DETECTION names the leading indicators and the logging discipline that makes drift visible in the same cycle, and OUT_OF_SCOPE_ROUTING gives the four destinations for out-of-scope work and the rule for choosing among them

competency_questions.question: When and how do I raise an existing client's monthly fee without ambushing them and without trading on their fear of losing their books?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REPRICING_CADENCE fixes the announced schedule and the evidence a change must rest on, REPRICE_CONVERSATION gives the notice, evidence and options structure, and CLIENT_CONDUCT_STANDARD forbids the pressure tactics that would otherwise make the increase land

competency_questions.question: What do I do about long-standing clients still paying an old fee for a scope that has quietly grown for years?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEGACY_PRICE_DEBT defines how the gap accumulates, how it is quantified per account, and the staged correction that avoids both a single punitive jump and permanent subsidy

competency_questions.question: How do I know whether the monthly reporting the client receives is actually read and used, and what do I change when it is not?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REPORT_USEFULNESS_LOOP names the evidence that a packet was used to make a decision, the failure signals of an unread packet, and the redesign moves available without crossing into advice that requires a licence

competency_questions.question: What belongs in the monthly review conversation, and at exactly what point must I stop and refer the owner to a licensed professional?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MONTHLY_REVIEW_CALL gives the agenda and the decision log, and ADVISORY_BOUNDARY_GUARD gives the recognizable trigger phrases, the stop-and-refer script, and the requirement to verify current rules in the practice jurisdiction

competency_questions.question: Which signals tell me a client is drifting toward cancellation, and which intervention matches which signal?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AT_RISK_SIGNAL_SET enumerates the observable signals with their lead time and false-positive risk, and RETENTION_INTERVENTION_LADDER maps each signal class to a proportionate response and to the point where saving the account stops being right

competency_questions.question: How do I handle a client whose business is in cash distress or who has stopped paying, without exploiting their situation and without subsidising them indefinitely?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISTRESSED_CLIENT_PROTOCOL states the care obligations, the transparent options, the work-stop and records-return boundary with its jurisdiction flag, and the point at which the account moves to the exit protocol

competency_questions.question: How do I price and staff a client whose business runs hard for part of the year and goes quiet for the rest, without losing them in the dead months?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEASONAL_CLIENT_TERMS gives the annualized-scope mechanism, the dormant-tier alternative and the pause rules with their capacity consequence, and WORKLOAD_CALENDAR_SMOOTHING shows how seasonal accounts are placed against the rest of the book

competency_questions.question: When is a client a mis-fit I should exit rather than keep saving, and how do I exit them without damaging their books or breaching confidentiality?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MISFIT_EXIT_PROTOCOL states the exit criteria decided in advance, the notice and handover sequence with the records the client is entitled to, and ACCESS_LIFECYCLE_DISCIPLINE states the credential revocation and data-retention steps that close the file

competency_questions.question: How do I build a steady referral flow from CPAs and niche communities without stepping on professional boundaries or leaking client information?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CPA_REFERRAL_ALLIANCE states the reciprocal mechanism, the boundary promise that makes a CPA safe to refer, and the client-authorization requirement before any information passes, and COMMUNITY_REFERRAL_ENGINE states how introductions are earned and asked for with consent and disclosure

competency_questions.question: What does the periodic review of the whole book have to decide, and what evidence proves the practice is healthy rather than merely busy?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOOK_HEALTH_REVIEW lists the composed inputs (capacity load, contribution, price debt, risk register, concentration) and the decisions the review must close with, and BOOK_ECONOMICS_MODEL supplies the identity that makes those inputs comparable

glossary.definition: The number of live subscription accounts one delivery seat can carry through a full monthly close cycle at the promised turnaround and accuracy, derived from that seat's measured monthly effort per account plus a reserve for absence, cleanup surprises and peak-week collision; a practice-specific measured quantity, never a figure borrowed from another firm.

The practice's own record of where recurring delivery time actually went per client per month, split at least into feed and reconciliation work, categorization judgment, chasing missing documents, reporting and review preparation, client communication, and unbilled goodwill tasks; it is the measurement instrument every capacity, contribution and repricing decision in this KB depends on.

A client's monthly subscription fee set against that client's measured cost-to-serve for the same month, expressed as a mechanism rather than a target number: fee minus delivery labour at the rate the practice is willing to sustain, minus the software, review and support overhead the account consumes; used to rank accounts and to detect subsidy, not to compute statutory profit.

The gradual entry of work into a live account that was never inside the tier the client bought - an extra entity, a new sales channel, a payroll run, a lender packet, a monthly call that became weekly - which is absorbed silently because each single instance is small and refusing feels petty.

The announced schedule on which every account's fee is compared against its measured scope and cost-to-serve, plus the named triggers that can move an individual account off-cycle; the cadence exists so that a fee change is a scheduled, evidenced event the client was told about at the start rather than a surprise reaction to a bad month.

The accumulated gap between what an early or long-standing client pays and what the same scope would be priced at today, created by years of small unpriced additions and skipped increases; it is quantified per account so the practice can decide between staged correction, scope reduction, or accepting the gap as a deliberate, named cost.

An observable behaviour that precedes cancellation with enough lead time to act on - reports never opened, documents arriving later each month, the review call repeatedly rescheduled, payment method failing, a new in-house hire or a new CPA appearing in the conversation, an owner asking what exactly they are paying for.

The slide from explaining what the books show into recommending what the owner should do about tax, entity structure, financing or legal exposure; it is the specific way a bookkeeping subscription walks into licensed territory, and it usually happens on a friendly monthly review call rather than in writing.

The mechanism by which a seasonal client's annual scope is priced as a level monthly subscription instead of a fee that collapses in quiet months, together with the alternative of an explicitly reduced dormant tier; the choice is stated in writing up front because the client experiences the level fee as paying for nothing in the quiet months.

The bundle handed to a departing client at exit: the ledger through the last closed period in a portable form, reconciliation status, the open-items list, where source documents live, what remains unfinished, and confirmation of which credentials the practice has relinquished; assembling it is the practice's obligation regardless of who ended the relationship or why.

nodes.definition: Hold one explicit model of how a subscription bookkeeping practice actually earns: recurring revenue is the sum of the monthly fees of the live accounts, and everything else is either a lever on that sum or a cost against it. There are only five levers and they are not interchangeable. Client count is bounded by delivery capacity, so it cannot be pushed without either adding a seat or lowering the promise. Tier mix moves revenue without moving headcount, but only if clients genuinely belong in the rungs they occupy. Fee level per rung moves revenue fastest and is the lever most likely to break the relationship if used carelessly. Cost-to-serve is the quietest lever, because a month of unnoticed absorbed work reduces earnings exactly as much as a fee cut of the same size while feeling like generosity. Retention multiplies all of the others, since an account kept is a month of revenue that costs no acquisition effort and a seat that stays productive. The model is stated as arithmetic the practice runs on its own measured numbers, never as an industry benchmark or a claimed multiple: no revenue-per-client, capacity or margin figure from an article or a peer belongs in this model as fact. Its job is to make every downstream decision in this KB comparable, so that firing a mis-fit client, correcting a legacy fee and declining an eager prospect can all be argued on the same terms.

included: the five levers and how each is bounded
cost-to-serve absorption stated as an earnings loss
retention as a multiplier on the other levers
the rule that all figures are measured in-practice, never borrowed
excluded: designing the tier ladder or its scope definitions
the practice's own tax, entity or statutory-accounts treatment
valuation of the practice or any account-multiple claim

pros.claim: One shared identity lets unrelated decisions be compared honestly instead of argued on instinct
pros.example: showing that keeping a chronically underwater restaurant client and declining a well-fitting trades prospect are the same decision made twice

pros.claim: Naming absorbed work as an earnings loss removes the illusion that goodwill is free
pros.example: a partner who calls two unbilled hours a month generosity sees it sitting in the same column as a fee reduction

cons.claim: An arithmetic frame can flatten relationship value that does not show up in a monthly number
cons.example: a small, barely-contributing client who has sent three good referrals from the same trade association

cons.claim: The model is only as honest as the effort measurement behind it, which does not exist yet when the model is first written
cons.example: a first pass built on remembered time that badly understates document chasing

failure_modes: treating client count as the only lever and hiring to chase revenue that better mix or corrected fees would have produced
importing a revenue-per-client or clients-per-seat figure from a podcast or peer group and treating it as this practice's number
leaving absorbed and goodwill work outside the model so cost-to-serve looks flat while it is rising
acceptance_tests: the model names all five levers, states which are capacity-bounded and which are relationship-bounded, and traces each to the node in this KB that governs it
every quantity in the model is sourced from the practice's own measurement or explicitly marked as an unverified estimate awaiting measurement
revisit_triggers: a seat is added, removed, or changes its share of delivery work
the tier ladder or its scope definitions change upstream
measured cost-to-serve moves materially for a whole niche cohort

base.update_signal: a full cycle of measured per-client effort and fee data that contradicts the assumed relationship between client count, mix and earnings

nodes.definition: Stand up a lightweight but honest record of the delivery effort each live account consumes each month, because nothing else in this subdomain can be decided from memory. The ledger splits a client-month into categories that behave differently: feed and reconciliation work, categorization judgment that needed thought rather than a rule, chasing missing documents and unanswered questions, report preparation and review-call preparation, ad-hoc client communication, and unbilled goodwill tasks that were done because refusing felt disproportionate. Categories matter more than precision: an account that is heavy because of chasing has a fixable client-behaviour problem, while an account that is heavy because of categorization judgment has a complexity problem that belongs in a different rung. Capture must be cheap enough to survive a busy close - a timer, a per-task tally, or a disciplined end-of-day note - and must run for at least one full cycle including a month-end and any quarter-end spike before its output is trusted. The ledger is a management instrument, not a billing record: the client is not billed by it, and it is never used to reconstruct a fee retroactively. Its outputs feed capacity derivation, contribution per client, drift detection and every repricing argument, which is why an estimate written from memory quietly corrupts all four at once.

included: effort categories that diagnose different causes
cheap capture that survives close week
a minimum observation window before the data is used
goodwill and absorbed work captured explicitly
excluded: billing the client by measured time or converting the subscription to hourly
the close checklist and its execution steps
staff performance evaluation or timesheet compliance management

pros.claim: Categorized effort tells you what is wrong with a heavy account, not just that it is heavy
pros.example: two accounts consuming similar time, one from document chasing and one from multi-entity categorization, needing opposite responses

pros.claim: A measured ledger converts every later pricing conversation from opinion into evidence the client can inspect
pros.example: showing an owner the count of document chases per month that came with their new second location

cons.claim: Capture discipline decays exactly when the book is busiest, which is when the data matters most
cons.example: a close week where nobody logs anything, leaving the heaviest month of the quarter invisible

cons.claim: Measuring time inside a fixed-fee practice can drag the team back into hourly thinking and defensive logging
cons.example: a bookkeeper padding the goodwill category to justify a slow month

failure_modes: logging a single undifferentiated total per client so no cause can be diagnosed
running the ledger for a quiet month and generalizing the result to the year
letting the ledger become a timesheet the team games or resents
leaving goodwill and unbilled favours out because they were not real work
acceptance_tests: every live account has at least one complete cycle of categorized effort captured, including a month-end and any quarter-end spike
goodwill and out-of-scope tasks appear as their own category with a count, not folded into general delivery time
the ledger is documented as a management instrument that is never used to bill or to reconstruct a past fee
revisit_triggers: a niche cohort's workload signature changes upstream
capture compliance drops below the level where a month can be trusted
a new software or automation change materially alters where time goes

base.update_signal: a completed measurement cycle whose category split differs materially from what the team believed before capture began

nodes.definition: Derive how many live accounts one delivery seat can carry as an output of measurement, and treat that derived number as a practice fact with an expiry date rather than a rule of thumb. The derivation starts from the seat's available delivery hours in a month after everything that is not client delivery has been removed - internal review, training, sales support, admin, and the hours that will be lost to absence over a year. From that base, subtract a reserve for the two things that reliably eat capacity: cleanup surprises inside accounts that were supposed to be steady, and the collision of close deadlines in the same week. What remains is divided by the measured effort of the accounts the seat actually holds, weighted by rung, not by an average client that does not exist. The result is a capacity band rather than a single number, because effort varies by rung and by month, and the band is expressed with the quality promise attached: this many accounts at this turnaround and this review depth. Capacity stated without the quality promise is meaningless, since any seat can hold more clients if the close slips or the review is skipped. The mechanism is re-run whenever the ledger updates, whenever a seat's non-delivery load changes, and whenever the mix of rungs on a seat shifts; a capacity number carried forward unchanged for a year is an assumption wearing the clothes of a measurement.

included: available delivery hours after non-delivery load
reserve for cleanup surprises and deadline collision
rung-weighted rather than average-client division
capacity as a band tied to a stated quality promise
excluded: hiring, contracting and compensation decisions for the seat
the close procedure the seat performs
publishing a clients-per-seat figure as an industry standard

pros.claim: A derived capacity band makes the intake decision arithmetic instead of a mood
pros.example: declining a fourth new client in a month because the seat holding them is already at the top of its band

pros.claim: Tying capacity to the quality promise exposes silent overloading before clients feel it
pros.example: noticing that the only way the current book fits is if reviews are skipped in the last week

cons.claim: Capacity derived from one period can be badly wrong for a book whose mix is changing
cons.example: a band computed on simple service clients before three inventory-heavy retailers were added

cons.claim: A stated ceiling invites the team to treat it as a target and fill it, leaving no slack for the unexpected
cons.example: a seat run at the top of its band when a long-standing client suddenly needs a lender packet

failure_modes: computing capacity on gross hours and ignoring review, admin and absence
using an average client when the seat holds a mix of rungs with different load
quoting a capacity number without the turnaround and review depth it assumed
never re-deriving after the book's composition changes
acceptance_tests: the capacity band is expressed as accounts per seat at a named turnaround and review depth, with the reserve stated separately
the derivation uses rung-weighted measured effort from the ledger rather than an average client
the band carries the date and the ledger window it was derived from and a recheck condition
revisit_triggers: the effort ledger updates for a cohort on that seat
a seat's non-delivery load changes materially
close turnaround slips for two consecutive cycles

base.update_signal: two consecutive cycles in which the seat delivered the promised turnaround with materially more or fewer accounts than the band predicted

nodes.definition: Put each account's monthly fee next to that account's measured cost-to-serve for the same month so subsidy inside the book becomes visible. Cost-to-serve is assembled as a mechanism, not a formula copied from elsewhere: the measured delivery effort valued at the labour rate the practice is willing to sustain for that seat, plus the software seats and integrations the account consumes, plus the review and support overhead it triggers, plus a share of the practice overhead allocated by a stated and consistent rule. What comes out is a ranking, not a profit figure - it is management arithmetic for deciding where to intervene, and it is never presented as statutory profit or shown to a client as one. Three patterns matter more than the ordering itself. An account underwater because of chasing and rework has a behaviour cause and often a fixable one. An account underwater because its real complexity outgrew its rung has a pricing cause and belongs in a rung conversation. An account underwater because it was priced low to win the logo in year one has a legacy cause and belongs in staged correction. The view is only trustworthy when the effort ledger behind it is, so a contribution ranking produced from remembered time will confidently point at the wrong clients, and firing decisions made from it will be wrong in exactly the cases that hurt most.

included: fee against measured cost-to-serve per account per month
a stated consistent overhead allocation rule
the three causes of an underwater account and where each one routes
use as an internal ranking only
excluded: statutory profit, tax or management accounts for the practice itself
showing per-client contribution figures to clients or in marketing
asserting any margin or benchmark figure as an industry norm

pros.claim: Ranking by contribution makes subsidy visible where averages hide it
pros.example: finding that two accounts absorb more delivery time than the four smallest accounts combined while paying the same rung fee

pros.claim: Separating cause from symptom prevents the reflex of firing a client who simply needs a rung move
pros.example: an underwater account that becomes healthy after its second entity is priced into the correct rung

cons.claim: Contribution is a monthly snapshot and punishes accounts whose value is lumpy or relational
cons.example: a seasonal wholesaler who looks terrible in three quiet months and carries the seat in the busy ones

cons.claim: Overhead allocation is a judgment call that can be tuned until it produces the answer someone wanted
cons.example: shifting software cost onto the accounts an owner already disliked

failure_modes: computing contribution from remembered rather than measured effort
changing the allocation rule between reviews so periods stop being comparable
treating a single bad month as a verdict on an account
letting a contribution ranking leak into a client conversation as if it were their profitability
acceptance_tests: every live account has a contribution line for the last completed cycle built from ledger effort and a written allocation rule
each underwater account carries a cause tag of behaviour, complexity or legacy and a routed next action
the allocation rule is unchanged since the previous review or its change is documented with the reason
revisit_triggers: the allocation rule or sustained labour rate changes
a rung's scope definition changes upstream
an account's cause tag changes after intervention

base.update_signal: a completed cycle in which contribution ranking reorders materially after effort is measured rather than estimated

nodes.definition: Keep an explicit, rehearsed line between explaining what the books show and telling an owner what to do about tax, entity structure, financing or legal exposure, because in a recurring relationship that line is crossed on friendly calls rather than in signed documents. The guard has three parts. First, recognition: a short list of the questions that actually arrive - should I switch entity type, can I write this off, should I take more salary or more distribution, will this look good enough for the lender, can you certify these numbers, should I put my spouse on payroll - and the recognition that each of these is a licensed judgment even when the arithmetic is easy and the owner is impatient. Second, the stop-and-refer move: state plainly what the books do show, name what the question actually is, say that it belongs to their tax professional or lawyer, and offer to prepare the ledger detail that professional will need. Third, documentation: the question, the referral and what was and was not said go in the account record, because the risky version of this conversation is the one nobody wrote down. The practice never signs off, certifies, attests to or opines on financial statements for a third party, and never characterizes a position as safe or allowable. Which activities are reserved, and what titles and wording the practice may use, differ by jurisdiction and change - verify current rules in your jurisdiction with a qualified professional rather than relying on habit or on what a peer in another region does.

included: the recognizable trigger questions in a live account
the stop-and-refer script and its documentation
the refusal to certify, attest or opine for a third party
the obligation to verify current jurisdiction rules
excluded: performing or reviewing the tax, attest or legal work itself
transaction-level judgment escalation inside the close, owned by the onboarding and close KB
advising the owner on which professional to appoint beyond offering more than one name

pros.claim: A rehearsed line lets the practice stay warm and useful without absorbing licensed risk
pros.example: answering a distribution-versus-salary question by showing the ledger history and handing the decision to the CPA the same day

pros.claim: Documenting the boundary moment turns a later dispute from memory into record
pros.example: a note showing the owner was told in writing that the write-off question was for their tax preparer

cons.claim: Refusing questions can read as unhelpful and is a genuine retention cost with owners who wanted one place to ask
cons.example: an owner who says their last bookkeeper always just told them what to do

cons.claim: The line is genuinely blurry in places, so consistent application requires judgment the team may not share
cons.example: disagreement over whether explaining how a category maps to a return line is explanation or advice

failure_modes: answering a tax or entity question because it seemed easy and the owner was anxious
signing, certifying or vouching for figures a lender or investor asked about
letting the boundary hold in writing but dissolve on the monthly call
assuming rules learned once still apply in the practice's current jurisdiction
acceptance_tests: the trigger-question list and the stop-and-refer script exist in writing and every delivery seat has rehearsed them
each boundary event in the last cycle appears in the account record with what was said and to whom it was referred
no client-facing artifact contains certification, assurance or opinion language, and the jurisdiction-verification note is present
revisit_triggers: a boundary incident or near miss occurs on any account
the practice adds a service that sits closer to licensed territory
regulatory or professional-body guidance in the practice jurisdiction is updated

base.update_signal: a change in professional or regulatory guidance in the practice jurisdiction, or a logged boundary incident showing the script failing in live use

nodes.definition: Treat the client credentials and financial data the practice holds as a standing liability to be managed for the whole life of the account and closed out at its end, not as an onboarding task that was completed once. The discipline covers four moments. Grant: access is requested at the lowest privilege that lets the work happen, through the client's own user management rather than shared logins, with each grant recorded against a named person and a named purpose. Hold: a periodic review confirms that every live grant still maps to someone who still works on that account, that credentials were never circulated by email or chat, and that any client who insists on sending a password receives the same corrective response every time. Change: staff turnover, a client's own system migration, or a seat reassignment triggers re-provisioning rather than password sharing. Close: at the end of a relationship, access is relinquished promptly, the client is told which accesses have been removed and confirms on their side, and retained working papers are kept only as long as the practice's documented retention position requires. Confidentiality runs alongside: nothing about an account - its name, its numbers, its troubles - is used in marketing, in a referral conversation, in a community post or in a proposal without the client's specific permission. Data-protection duties, breach-notification triggers and records-retention periods differ by jurisdiction and change, so the practice names the obligation class and verifies current rules locally rather than assuming.

included: least-privilege grant through the client's own user management
periodic review of live grants against current staffing
re-provisioning on staff or system change
prompt revocation and confirmation at exit
consent before any client information is used externally
excluded: security tooling selection and IT infrastructure administration
the close-process controls that check accuracy of the ledger
legal interpretation of a breach or of retention statutes, which is referred out

pros.claim: A lifecycle view catches the access that quietly outlives its purpose
pros.example: a quarterly review finding a departed bookkeeper still holding banking view rights on four accounts

pros.claim: Clean revocation at exit removes the single most common post-exit dispute
pros.example: a departing client receiving a written confirmation of every credential relinquished on the day of handover

cons.claim: Least-privilege provisioning is slower and friction with clients who want to hand over one shared login is constant
cons.example: an owner who keeps offering the master password because it is easier than adding a user

cons.claim: Periodic access review is unglamorous work that competes directly with close-week delivery
cons.example: a review deferred three months running because month-end always arrived first

failure_modes: accepting shared master credentials because the client offered them
leaving grants in place after staff or seat changes
naming a client or their situation in a referral or marketing conversation without permission
keeping working papers indefinitely with no documented retention position
acceptance_tests: every live access grant maps to a named current person, a named purpose and a client-side user record rather than a shared login
the access review ran within its stated interval and produced revocations or an explicit nil return
each closed account has a dated revocation confirmation and a retention decision on file
revisit_triggers: any staffing change on a delivery seat
a client migrates accounting or banking systems
a suspected exposure, misdirected file or credential incident
data-protection or retention guidance in the practice jurisdiction changes

base.update_signal: an access review or incident showing grants outliving their purpose, or a change in data-protection or retention obligations in the practice jurisdiction

nodes.definition: Fix in advance how the practice is allowed to talk to a client whose money or continuation is at stake, so that conduct does not become situational when revenue is on the line. Four commitments hold across every pricing, save, downgrade and exit conversation. Disclosure first: a fee change, a scope reduction, a policy change or a termination is put in writing before it is discussed, with the effective date and the notice period the engagement terms require, and never applied retroactively to a period already delivered. No fear-selling: the practice does not imply that the owner's books will collapse, that they will face penalties, or that nobody else will take them on; the case for staying is made from what the service does, and any statement about consequences is limited to what the practice can actually observe in the ledger. Care with owners under strain: when an owner is in cash distress, bereaved, ill, or clearly overwhelmed, the practice slows the conversation down, puts options in writing, avoids same-call commitments, and does not use a moment of panic to close an upgrade. Symmetry: any concession offered to keep a client - a discount, a pause, a deferred increase - is written with its end date and its condition, so a save does not silently become a permanent secret price. These are constraints, not preferences: they bind even when the client would have said yes to the faster, harder version, and a save achieved outside them is treated as a failure to be unwound rather than a result to be repeated.

included: written-first disclosure with effective date and notice period
prohibition on fear framing and consequence claims beyond the ledger
slowed process and written options for owners under strain
every concession dated and conditioned
excluded: the pre-engagement sales conversation with a prospect, owned by the offer and niche selection KB
drafting or interpreting the engagement contract itself, which is a legal question referred out
debt collection litigation or third-party collection agency conduct

pros.claim: A fixed conduct standard removes the temptation to improvise pressure in the month a client is lost
pros.example: an increase delivered in writing two cycles ahead rather than raised on a call after a bad close

pros.claim: Written, dated concessions prevent the slow accumulation of invisible discounts across the book
pros.example: a two-cycle pause that expires automatically instead of becoming a permanent lower fee nobody remembers agreeing

cons.claim: Disclosure-first is slower and sometimes loses a client who would have stayed under a faster, more persuasive approach
cons.example: an owner who takes the written notice as a prompt to shop around

cons.claim: Judging when an owner is under strain is subjective and can slide into paternalism or inconsistent treatment
cons.example: slowing down for one distressed owner while pushing a decision on another who hid it better

failure_modes: raising a fee change verbally on a call and confirming in writing afterwards
hinting that a departing client's books will fall apart or that penalties are likely
closing an upgrade in the same conversation where an owner disclosed a cash crisis
granting an undated goodwill discount that quietly becomes the permanent price
acceptance_tests: every fee, scope or termination change in the last cycle was issued in writing with an effective date and the contractual notice period before it was discussed
no client-facing message in the last cycle contains a consequence claim the practice cannot evidence from that client's own ledger
every live concession has a written end date and condition
revisit_triggers: a complaint, dispute or negative exit citing pressure or surprise
engagement terms or notice periods change
a save is achieved by an exception outside the standard

base.update_signal: a logged complaint, dispute or exit reason alleging surprise or pressure, or a change in the engagement terms governing notice

nodes.definition: Manage the shape of the load, not only its total, because a book that fits comfortably on average can be undeliverable in the last week of the month. Two shapes matter. The monthly shape is created by every client wanting their reporting soon after period end, by feeds and statements arriving on different days, and by the practice's own review step needing to sit before delivery; left unmanaged it concentrates the whole book into a few days and turns every small surprise into a missed promise. The yearly shape is created by client seasonality, by year-end work, and by the period when clients and their tax professionals need information at once. Smoothing works through a small number of levers: staggering promised delivery dates across cohorts rather than promising the same date to everyone, sequencing accounts by when their source data reliably lands rather than by client importance, placing seasonal clients whose peaks fall in opposite quarters on the same seat, keeping a deliberate gap in the calendar for the cleanup surprise that arrives every month in some account, and assigning any account with an immovable external deadline where it does not collide with several others. Smoothing decisions are recorded per account, since the promise a client received is part of the account's terms and cannot be quietly moved to make a busy week fit. When smoothing can no longer absorb the shape, the honest conclusion is that capacity, not scheduling, is the constraint.

included: staggered promised delivery dates across cohorts
sequencing by data arrival reliability
pairing counter-seasonal clients on a seat
deliberate slack for the recurring surprise
recording the promise per account
excluded: the close checklist itself and its internal steps
staff rostering, employment terms and leave policy
changing a client's promised date without the notice their terms require

pros.claim: Staggering converts a book that only fits in theory into one that fits every week
pros.example: moving a cohort of service clients to a mid-month delivery date because their bank feeds settle earlier

pros.claim: Counter-seasonal pairing lets one seat carry more accounts without a quality cut
pros.example: placing a landscaping client with a summer peak alongside a retailer whose peak is the holiday quarter

cons.claim: Clients experience a staggered date as slower service and some will push back hard
cons.example: an owner who wants numbers on the third day because their previous provider promised it

cons.claim: Smoothing can disguise a genuine capacity shortfall for months until it collapses in one bad cycle
cons.example: a book that only ever fits because two people worked every weekend in close week

failure_modes: promising the same delivery date to every client regardless of cohort
sequencing by who complains loudest instead of by when their data lands
leaving no slack, so one cleanup surprise cascades into several missed promises
moving a promised date without notice to rescue an overloaded week
acceptance_tests: each account has a recorded promised delivery date and a data-arrival assumption behind it
the calendar shows deliberate slack in close week rather than being fully committed
no promised date was changed in the last cycle without written notice to the client
revisit_triggers: two or more promised dates are missed in the same cycle
a cohort's data-arrival pattern changes
a seasonal client is added, exits or changes its peak
a seat gains or loses accounts

base.update_signal: a cycle in which promised dates were missed despite the book sitting inside its capacity band, indicating the shape rather than the total is binding

nodes.definition: Put a standing gate between a sold client and a delivery seat, so that admission is a capacity decision made by the practice rather than a consequence of someone having said yes. The gate asks four questions in order. Is there room in the target seat's capacity band after the reserve, counting the incoming account at its measured rung load rather than its optimistic one? Does the account's shape fit the calendar it is joining, or does it land another immovable deadline in an already crowded week? Does admitting it push any existing account past its promised delivery date, since capacity spent on a new client is capacity taken from clients who are already paying? And is the seat's current book stable enough to absorb a new account's first months, which always cost more than steady state? When the answers do not clear the gate, the honest options are a start date in a later cycle, admission onto a different seat, or a queue with a stated position and an honest expectation - never a quiet admission that will be paid for by the existing book. The gate is also the point at which capacity released by an exit becomes available, and the point where a referral surge from a good month meets reality. It is deliberately unpopular with whoever sold the work, which is why the rule is written down, applied the same way every month, and reported at the book review rather than negotiated case by case.

included: the four admission questions and their order
deferral, reassignment or an honest queue as the only alternatives
first-months cost counted against capacity
release of capacity by exits flowing back through the gate
excluded: qualifying, pricing or selling the prospect, owned by the offer and niche selection KB
the onboarding and cleanup project once admission is granted
declining a prospect for fit reasons unrelated to capacity

pros.claim: A written gate protects paying clients from the cost of the next sale
pros.example: deferring a start date by one cycle rather than letting three existing accounts slip their promised week

pros.claim: An honest queue converts overflow demand into future revenue instead of a damaged first month
pros.example: telling a referred prospect they can start after the quarter with a firm date rather than starting them badly now

cons.claim: Deferring admission risks losing prospects to a competitor who will start immediately
cons.example: a referred owner who cannot wait a cycle and goes elsewhere

cons.claim: The gate creates real internal conflict between whoever sold the work and whoever must deliver it
cons.example: a partner pushing an exception for a strategically attractive logo

failure_modes: admitting on optimism about the account's load rather than its rung-weighted measured effort
counting only steady-state effort and ignoring the heavier first months
granting exceptions for attractive clients until the gate means nothing
leaving a queue unmanaged so waiting prospects hear nothing and drift away
acceptance_tests: every admission in the last cycle records the seat, the remaining band headroom and the four gate answers
no admission in the last cycle coincided with a missed promised date on an existing account of that seat
queued prospects have a stated position and a communicated expectation
revisit_triggers: the capacity band is re-derived
an exit releases capacity
referral inflow exceeds what the gate can admit for two consecutive cycles
an exception is granted

base.update_signal: a cycle in which admissions cleared the gate but existing accounts still slipped, or in which repeated exceptions show the gate is not being applied

nodes.definition: Build the sensing that catches work entering an account that the client never bought, while it is still one task rather than an established habit. Drift is rarely announced; it arrives as an extra bank account nobody mentioned, a second entity whose transactions started appearing in the same file, a new sales channel with its own payout structure, a payroll run that was supposed to be a one-off, a lender or investor packet requested at short notice, a weekly call that grew out of a monthly one, or a stream of small questions that now occupy an hour a week. The detection instruments are deliberately mundane: the effort ledger showing an account's hours climbing without a rung change, the goodwill category filling up with tasks nobody priced, a count of source items or channels that no longer matches what the tier assumed, close notes repeatedly mentioning something new, and the delivery team's own irritation, which is usually the earliest signal of all. Detection has a timing rule, because it is the timing that decides everything downstream: drift is named in the cycle it appears, when the conversation is a small factual observation, not at the annual review, when it has become the client's reasonable expectation and naming it feels like a takeaway. Detection stops at naming and evidencing; deciding what happens to the work is the routing decision, and the two are kept separate so that seeing drift does not depend on being ready to charge for it.

included: the recurring shapes drift arrives in
ledger, count and narrative instruments that surface it
the same-cycle naming rule
separation of detection from the pricing decision
excluded: defining the tier scope that drift is measured against, owned by the offer and niche selection KB
the close checklist steps that process the work
deciding the destination for the work, which is the routing node

pros.claim: Same-cycle detection keeps the conversation factual instead of confrontational
pros.example: mentioning a newly appeared second bank account in the current month's summary rather than after six months of quietly reconciling it

pros.claim: Counting scope units against what the tier assumed makes drift arguable from evidence, not from feeling
pros.example: showing that transaction volume and channel count both moved after a marketplace launch

cons.claim: Constant scope vigilance can make a practice feel petty to clients who value flexibility
cons.example: an owner who hears every observation as a prelude to an invoice

cons.claim: Detection depends on ledger discipline that decays in busy months, exactly when drift is most likely
cons.example: a quarter-end where extra work was absorbed and never logged

failure_modes: noticing drift only when the annual review shows the account underwater
treating each instance as a one-off favour so the pattern never accumulates anywhere
logging drift privately and never surfacing it to the client
conflating detection with confrontation so nobody raises it
acceptance_tests: each live account has a current scope-unit count and a drift log covering the last completed cycle
every drift item logged in the cycle has a date, an evidence note and a named destination decision or an explicit deferral
the goodwill category is non-empty or its emptiness is explained, since an empty goodwill log usually means nobody is recording
revisit_triggers: an account's effort rises for two consecutive cycles without a rung change
a client's business changes structure, adds an entity, a location or a channel
the same drift class appears across several accounts in a niche

base.update_signal: a cycle in which drift was found only in retrospect, showing the sensing instruments missed it while it was still one task

nodes.definition: Give every piece of out-of-scope work exactly one of four destinations, decided deliberately and recorded, so that nothing lands in the fifth destination that quietly destroys a fixed-fee practice: silent absorption. The first destination is a priced add-on, used when the work is real, repeatable and outside the rung, and it is offered with its price before it is done rather than invoiced afterwards. The second is a rung move, used when the work is not an exception but evidence that the account now lives in a different tier; the trigger is the account's scope units crossing what the tier assumed, not the client's mood. The third is a named goodwill instance, used sparingly for work that is small, genuinely one-off, and worth absorbing for the relationship - and logged as goodwill precisely so the practice can see how often it is choosing this. The fourth is a decline with a referral, used when the work belongs to someone else entirely: tax positions, attest or assurance, legal interpretation, or specialist areas the practice does not deliver. The routing rule is a sequence, not a preference: check the licensed boundary first, because work that requires a licence is never eligible to be an add-on however profitable it looks; then check whether the pattern is recurring, because recurring work belongs in a rung rather than in an endless string of add-ons; then price or absorb consciously. The client hears the destination in plain terms with the reason, and the decision goes in the account record so the next instance does not restart the argument.

included: the four destinations and the order they are tested in
price-before-doing for add-ons
recurring work routed to a rung rather than repeated add-ons
goodwill logged as a conscious choice
excluded: designing the add-on catalogue or the rung definitions, owned by the offer and niche selection KB
performing the licensed work that is declined
the fee-level derivation itself, which follows the practice pricing mechanism

pros.claim: A fixed destination set ends the case-by-case improvisation that leaks margin
pros.example: a lender packet request answered the same way for every client instead of absorbed for the ones who ask nicely

pros.claim: Pricing before doing keeps the client in control and avoids surprise invoices
pros.example: quoting the extra entity reconciliation before the first month of it is performed

cons.claim: Naming a price for small requests can feel transactional and damage a warm relationship
cons.example: an owner who stops asking useful questions because they fear each one carries a charge

cons.claim: Routing decisions require judgment about whether something is genuinely recurring, and getting it wrong creates churn between rungs
cons.example: moving a client up a rung on the strength of a temporary project that ends two months later

failure_modes: absorbing silently because the moment to speak passed
accepting licensed work as a paid add-on because the client offered to pay for it
stacking repeated add-ons for work that clearly belongs in a higher rung
granting goodwill without logging it, so the pattern is invisible at review
acceptance_tests: every drift item from the last cycle carries one of the four destinations with a date and a reason
no item routed to add-on or goodwill would have failed the licensed-boundary test
no account shows the same add-on class three cycles running without a rung review being opened
revisit_triggers: the same out-of-scope class recurs across a niche cohort
goodwill instances exceed the practice tolerance in a cycle
a client disputes an add-on price or its timing

base.update_signal: a review of routed items showing a rising share absorbed as goodwill or repeated add-ons standing in for an overdue rung move
